title: The day's schedule under the arc
question: The fan you chose, with the space under it filled by today's plan. The items are samples, but their shape is exactly what dpAll() already returns in the app - what, which hour, how long - so this ports as a swap of the source rather than a redesign. Three ways to show it.

options.label: A · the next three
options.thesis: What is still ahead, first, as rows in the same rhythm as the meal pills. Anything already done is pressed into the surface instead of raised, so the day reads as a stack that empties.
options.risk: It shows three of however many the day holds, so a full day is silently cut. And 07:00 appearing under 20:00 - because done items sink to the bottom - reads oddly until you know the rule.

options.label: B · the day as a ribbon
options.thesis: The whole day at once, in order, as four small cards. Done ones are pressed in; what is left stands out.
options.risk: The names are cut at this width - פגישה עם נ… - and a day with six items would have to scroll sideways, which hides things on a home screen.

options.label: C · an hour rail
options.thesis: A pressed channel for the whole day with a lit dot at each item, and only the next one named. The quietest: it says when, not what, until it matters.
options.viewport: A rail of dots, and one named row.
options.risk: The lit dots are amber, which is the colour you reserved. It can be any other hue - say which.
